specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: A statement fails inside a transaction and its top-level ROLLBACK fails on the client; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). Then arm the client-side fault: the next top-level ROLLBACK fails in the driver and is not sent.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API, and do not catch the error. It fails with unique_violation (23505), which aborts the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK, which fails, so the connection stays in its aborted transaction block.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: MikroORM's defaults: em.transactional(callback) in a RequestContext, allowGlobalContext false. One non-default option is part of a case's form, not of the mode: the TX-02 cases call the nested em.transactional() with { clear: true }, as the reused experiments did, and each result records that form and its reason.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside unit 1, which aborts its transaction, then a client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): the top-level ROLLBACK fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.injection_point: The framework's ROLLBACK of unit 1, after the failed statement.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture). The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: Unit 1's transaction is already aborted: pg_xact_status() reports it aborted, and it holds no locks. Its connection stays in the aborted transaction block ("idle in transaction (aborted)"), where every statement except ROLLBACK fails with 25P02.
fault.expected_client: The unique violation, then an error from the framework's rollback; what the framework then does with the connection is under test. A unit of work given the connection as it is fails loudly with 25P02, instead of silently joining the open transaction as in TX-03.rollback-not-sent.

knowledge: The framework received PostgreSQL's error for the failed statement, and knows that its ROLLBACK failed, so it knows that the connection is still inside a transaction block.

api_outcome.basis: em.transactional(callback) rejected with the error the callback threw
api_outcome.contract: In MikroORM 7.2.5, em.transactional(callback) runs the callback, flushes, and commits (AbstractSqlConnection.transactional in @mikro-orm/sql: begin, callback, commit, return); if the callback or the flush throws, it rolls back and rethrows that error. A resolved call is MikroORM's report that the transaction committed.

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
unit 1's failing statement failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the next unit of work was attempted
the withheld ROLLBACK left unit 1's aborted transaction block in place: its session was "idle in transaction (aborted)", with no backend_xid, and pg_xact_status() already reported unit 1 aborted
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction (aborted)", backend_xid NULL; transactionid locks []; unit 1 pg_xact_status: aborted
